passages.note: House Third Reading vote page names her Aye and the divided tally but prints no provision.
Bill overview lists her as a co-sponsor of the gestational-limit bill; she served in the House of this legislature in 2022, so V5 option B makes it in-term.

passages.provision_quote: Except in a medical emergency, a physician may not intentionally or knowingly perform, induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion if the probable gestational age of the unborn human being has been determined to be greater than fifteen weeks.
passages.note: Chapter text of the instrument she co-sponsored and voted for; its Construction section disclaims any permitted stage before the limit.

rows.reasoning: SB 1164 (2022) sets a fifteen-week limit with a medical-emergency exception that reaches "serious risk of substantial and irreversible impairment of a major bodily function", which would otherwise read on the rung allowing abortion during the first trimester and after that only to protect the mother's health. But its Construction section says the act does not "Create or recognize a right to abortion" and that "The Legislature does not intend this act to make lawful an abortion that is currently unlawful", nor does it "Repeal, by implication or otherwise, section 13-3603, Arizona Revised Statutes, or any other applicable state law regulating or restricting abortion" — so it evidences no permitted stage, only the restrictive side (annex rung 3, ruled 2026-10-01). Her co-sponsorship and Aye vote therefore place her on that side without separating the rungs on it.
needs_source: An Arizona record or her own first-person words showing what stage of pregnancy she would permit abortion in, and which exceptions apply after it (SB 1164's construction clause leaves the permitted stage unevidenced)
